followup_explanation:
My reasoning:

This is a well-specified text-improvement/copyediting task with clear constraints (improve the prose, preserve wiki style, don't "mangle" the content). It's essentially editing and reformatting existing structured content—not open-ended creative generation.

On the deciding factors:

- **Capability:** Petrel leads or ties Plover across every internal eval category, including the most relevant ones here—Summarization (86.4 vs 80.6) and Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7, though that gap is near the variance threshold). Petrel also has stronger benchmark scores across the board (IFEval 89.8 vs 85.3 matters for "follow these instructions carefully" tasks). There's no category where Plover has a real edge.

- **Task preferences:** Plover self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work and prefers tightly-specified reformatting tasks—which might seem to favor it here. But the documentation is explicit that this preference is *dissociated from measured capability*, so it shouldn't drive the routing decision. Petrel's only notable preference trait (tolerance for distasteful content) is irrelevant to this benign editing request.

Since capability is the thing that actually predicts output quality and Petrel is at least as good everywhere—and clearly better on the summarization/instruction-following axes this task leans on—Petrel is the stronger choice.
